title: Conormal sequence of a section of a smooth algebra is exact
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $C$ a commutative ring with a surjective ring map $A\to C$, and $\beta:B\to C$ a ring map whose composite with $A\to B$ is $A\to C$ (so $\beta$ is surjective). Put $I=\ker(A\to C)$ and $J=\ker\beta$; then $I/I^2$ and $J/J^2$ are $C$-modules ($C=A/I=B/J$). Then the sequence of $C$-modules $$0\to I/I^2\xrightarrow{\ u\ }J/J^2\xrightarrow{\ v\ }\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\to0$$ is exact, where $u$ is induced by $A\to B$ and $v(b\bmod J^2)=\mathrm db\otimes1$ ($\Omega_{B/A}$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 06A9 (lemma-application-NL-smooth, line 38386), the sequence and maps being those of Lemma Tag 065V (lemma-application-NL, line 35519)

proof.text: *The maps $u$, $v$; $v\circ u=0$; $v$ surjective.* Write $\varphi:A\to B$ and $\pi:A\to C$, so $\beta\circ\varphi=\pi$; then $\varphi(I)\subseteq J$, hence $\varphi(I^2)\subseteq J^2$, and $u(a\bmod I^2)=\varphi(a)\bmod J^2$ is well defined and additive; it is $C$-linear because for $x\in A$ the element $\varphi(x)$ acts on $J/J^2$ by $\beta(\varphi(x))=\pi(x)$. The map $b\mapsto\mathrm db\otimes1$ on $J$ is additive and kills $J^2$: for $b,b'\in J$, $\mathrm d(bb')\otimes1=\mathrm db'\otimes\beta(b)+\mathrm db\otimes\beta(b')=0$ (Leibniz rule); it is $C$-linear since $\mathrm d(yb)\otimes1=\mathrm db\otimes\beta(y)+\mathrm dy\otimes\beta(b)=\beta(y)(\mathrm db\otimes1)$ for $y\in B$, $b\in J$. So $v$ is a well defined $C$-linear map. $v\circ u=0$ because $\mathrm d(\varphi(a))=0$ for $a\in A$ ($\mathrm d$ is an $A$-derivation). $v$ is surjective: the $C$-module $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC$ is generated by the elements $\mathrm db\otimes1$, $b\in B$ ($\Omega_{B/A}$ is generated by the $\mathrm db$); given $b$, choose $a\in A$ with $\pi(a)=\beta(b)$ ($\pi$ surjective); then $b-\varphi(a)\in J$ and $v\bigl((b-\varphi(a))\bmod J^2\bigr)=\mathrm db\otimes1$. (Also $\beta$ is surjective since $\pi=\beta\circ\varphi$ is.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065V (lemma-application-NL, line 35519): the sequence and its maps; the verifications are written out by the agent

proof.text: *A section $\sigma:B\to A/I^2$.* Make $D=A/I^2$ an $A$-algebra by the quotient map; $N=I/I^2\subseteq D$ is an ideal with $N^2=0$, and $D/N=A/I$, which $\pi$ identifies with $C$, so that the quotient map $q:D\to D/N$ becomes $a\bmod I^2\mapsto\pi(a)$. The map $\beta:B\to C=D/N$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras ($\beta\circ\varphi=\pi$). Since $A\to B$ is smooth, $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{B/A}$ is projective [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] there is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\sigma:B\to A/I^2$ with $q\circ\sigma=\beta$; being an $A$-algebra map, $\sigma(\varphi(a))=a\bmod I^2$ for $a\in A$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 06A7 (lemma-application-NL-formally-smooth, line 38079), first sentence, with Proposition Tag 00TN as used in the proof of Lemma Tag 06A9 (line 38386)

proof.text: *$u$ has a $C$-linear left inverse, so $u$ is injective.* For $b\in J$, $q(\sigma(b))=\beta(b)=0$, so $\sigma(b)\in I/I^2$; for $b,b'\in J$, $\sigma(bb')=\sigma(b)\sigma(b')\in(I/I^2)^2=0$, so $\sigma(J^2)=0$. Hence $r:J/J^2\to I/I^2$, $r(b\bmod J^2)=\sigma(b)$, is well defined and additive; it is $C$-linear because for $y\in B$, $\sigma(yb)=\sigma(y)\sigma(b)$ and $\sigma(y)\in A/I^2$ acts on $I/I^2$ through its image $q(\sigma(y))=\beta(y)\in C$. For $a\in I$, $r(u(a\bmod I^2))=\sigma(\varphi(a))=a\bmod I^2$ by step 2, so $r\circ u=\mathrm{id}_{I/I^2}$ and $u$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 06A7 (line 38079), second sentence ($\sigma$ induces a map $J/J^2\to I/I^2$ inverse to $I/I^2\to J/J^2$, i.e. a left inverse)

proof.text: *Exactness at $J/J^2$.* Let $\iota:A/I^2\to B/J^2$ be the ring map induced by $\varphi$ ($\varphi(I^2)\subseteq J^2$); on $I/I^2$ it is $u$. Define $\delta:B\to J/J^2$ by $\delta(b)=\bar b-\iota(\sigma(b))$, $\bar b$ the class of $b$ in $B/J^2$; this lies in $J/J^2$ because both terms map to $\beta(b)$ in $B/J=C$ (the second as $q(\sigma(b))=\beta(b)$). $\delta$ is additive, $\delta(\varphi(a))=\overline{\varphi(a)}-\iota(a\bmod I^2)=0$ for $a\in A$, and for $b,b'\in B$, in $B/J^2$: $\overline{bb'}-\iota\sigma(b)\,\iota\sigma(b')=\bar b\,\delta(b')+\iota\sigma(b')\,\delta(b)$, where $\bar b$ and $\iota\sigma(b')$ act on the $B/J$-module $J/J^2$ through $\beta(b)$ and $\beta(b')$; so $\delta(bb')=b\,\delta(b')+b'\,\delta(b)$ for the $B$-module structure of $J/J^2$ via $\beta$. Hence $\delta$ is an $A$-derivation of $B$ into the $B$-module $J/J^2$, and by the universal property of $(\Omega_{B/A},\mathrm d)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] there is a $B$-linear $\theta:\Omega_{B/A}\to J/J^2$ with $\theta\circ\mathrm d=\delta$; since $J/J^2$ is a $C$-module, $\theta$ induces a $C$-linear $s:\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\to J/J^2$, $s(\omega\otimes c)=c\,\theta(\omega)$. For $b\in J$ and $x=b\bmod J^2$: $s(v(x))=\delta(b)=x-\iota(\sigma(b))=x-u(r(x))$, since $\sigma(b)\in I/I^2$ (step 3). So $x=u(r(x))+s(v(x))$ for all $x\in J/J^2$, and if $v(x)=0$ then $x=u(r(x))$ lies in the image of $u$. With $v\circ u=0$ (step 1), $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 06A7 (line 38079): Stacks takes exactness at $J/J^2$ from Lemma Tag 065V (line 35519, via the Jacobi-Zariski sequence 00S2 and Lemma 07BP); this step instead derives it from the section $\sigma$ of step 2 (written by the agent; it also shows the sequence is split, as 06A7 states)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 3 the sequence is exact at $I/I^2$, by step 4 at $J/J^2$, and by step 1 ($v$ surjective) at $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC$. So $0\to I/I^2\xrightarrow{u}J/J^2\xrightarrow{v}\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BC\to0$ is exact (indeed split exact, with $r$ and $s$ as splittings).
